intro.es: Lee entre líneas: identifica postura, concesiones y supuestos del autor.

mission.es: Distingue lo que el autor afirma de la posición que deja entrever.

content.targetText: When the regional museum reopened its collection, the oldest map carried two labels. The familiar one identified its maker and date; the new one explained that the map had been drawn for a trading company whose routes depended on forced labour. Some visitors praised the addition as overdue context. Others complained that an object should not be made to answer for a whole political history. The curator did not remove the first label. She argued that precision and context were different obligations, and that fulfilling one did not cancel the other. Yet the revised display exposed a harder question. A short label can acknowledge exploitation without explaining how the museum acquired the map, who has asked for access to it, or why a digital copy is easier to view than the original. The museum promised to publish its acquisition records, but only after verifying names in documents that often recorded workers as numbers. A critic called the delay another form of silence; the curator called it a refusal to replace one simplification with another. Neither position settles what the visitor sees today: two labels, a map, and an empty space where a fuller account might eventually appear.
